simulation_model: operands and stored results rounded to fp16/bf16 (RNE), fp32 accumulation and epilogue, one rounding per stored matrix; reference = fp64 SVD polar of the rounded input

cost_model.units: n^3 with n = min(m, N), alpha = max/min dimension
cost_model.sym: SYRK alpha, Q@X 2 alpha, symmetric n x n product 1; Gram quintic pass of T steps = 4T-3 products
cost_model.dense: Gram 2 alpha, Q@X 2 alpha, n x n product 2

caveats: All accuracy numbers are from fp16/bf16 rounding emulation on CPU (fp32 accumulate), not GPU kernels; no wall-clock latency is measured.
Test matrices are synthetic (random singular vectors, prescribed spectra); real Muon momentum (T1-02) has not been used, so the achievable ell after spectral scaling is unverified.
Polar Express baselines are re-derived greedy circuits, not the official coefficient list. Polar Switch is compared by the brief's FLOP formula only; PS3-55 is not compared.
FLOPs use the 'sym' model (symmetric n x n products at n^3); the 'dense' model is also reported.
A spectral circuit is only valid for sigma_min / sigma_hat >= ell; below that, directions are partially orthogonalized (bounded, not polished).
0-restart Gram circuits are unstable in bf16 for T >= 4: rounding makes Gram eigenvalues negative and y -> y h(y)^2 amplifies them by a_t^2 per step.
